message.content: I'll raise cash on Indiana first so the orange set can be built this turn.
message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I just completed a trade for the orange monopoly. I now own ST_JAMES_PLACE, TENNESSEE_AVENUE, and NEW_YORK_AVENUE. I have $162 in cash.

Virginia Avenue is no longer in my holdings. I still own Vermont, Indiana, the Electric Company, and Water Works. No houses are built yet.

One house on the orange monopoly costs $100. I can build it with my $162 cash, leaving $62. Rent with one house is $90 for St. James and Tennessee, and $100 for New York. Without houses the orange rent is only $20 to $24. Building one house would leave me vulnerable.

Player 3 owns all four railroads and charges $200 rent. With only $62 left after building one house, I cannot afford that hit without mortgaging. I am checking the mortgage values for my properties.

Mortgage values for my properties are now clear. Vermont is $50, Indiana $110, Electric and Water $75 each, St. James and Tennessee $90 each, and New York $100. Building one house would leave only $62 cash, which is too little to survive a $200 railroad rent without mortgaging. I need to plan how to mortgage enough to stay afloat.

Mortgaging the utilities, Vermont, and Indiana would raise $310. Combined with my $162 cash, I would have $472 total. Three houses on the orange monopoly cost $300, leaving $172. That is still too little to survive a $200 railroad rent. Four houses would cost $400 and leave only $72. This path does not solve the cash shortfall.

The maximum legal house count is four, but that would cost $400 and leave only $72 cash. Even with all mortgages raised, the total would be $472. With current cash alone, I can only afford one house without mortgaging.

I am weighing whether to mortgage properties before building houses. The action is limited to one tool call. I must act quickly because the orange monopoly is a high-traffic zone after jail. Player 3 owns all four railroads and several other valuable properties, making him a severe threat.

Player 4 wants to trade States and Virginia for Park Place to complete the pink and dark blue monopolies. This would leave me facing two monopolies plus four railroads. I should try to disrupt this deal. I own Indiana, which is part of the red set, but that set is not easily completed.

Mortgaging Indiana, Vermont, and one utility would raise $235. Combined with my cash, I would have $397 total. Building three houses on the orange monopoly would cost $300 and leave $97. This is a safer path than building one house with only $62 remaining.

Three houses still leaves only $172 cash. That is $28 short of the $200 buffer needed to survive a railroad rent. I cannot mortgage an orange property that already has houses on it. I must sell those houses first before mortgaging.

Selling one house would return $50, leaving $222 after a $200 railroad rent. That is survivable but painful. Two houses on the orange set would cost $200 and leave a $272 buffer. I am now verifying the exact standard rent values for each house count.

I corrected the standard Monopoly rent values. St. James Place and Tennessee Avenue each cost $180 and rent $70 with one house, $200 with two, $550 with three, and $750 with four. New York Avenue costs $200 and rents $80 with one house, $220 with two, $600 with three, and $800 with four.

Three houses on the orange set would generate $550 to $600 in rent. That is devastatingly high. Opponents would likely avoid the area or go bankrupt.

Two houses would be too weak to stop opponents. Three houses are the right call because the expected value is huge and players leaving jail often land on orange. I will mortgage non-essential properties to raise cash, then build three houses.

I will mortgage first and build houses in a second action. The utilities are poor income sources, so I will not keep them unmortgaged. Vermont does not block player 2's light blue set, since Connecticut is owned by player 2 and Oriental is in the bank.

Mortgaging does not transfer ownership, so I will keep Vermont and Indiana mortgaged to block player 2 and player 3 from completing their monopolies. I will mortgage all four non-orange properties first, then build three houses, then end my turn. This raises $472 in cash.

Two houses would leave $272 cash, which is safe against a $200 railroad hit. The rent would only be $70 to $80, so it would not bankrupt the other players. Three houses generate $550 to $600 in rent, which is devastatingly strong and worth the thin margin.

I am now considering trading before building houses. Player 4 wants to trade States and Virginia for Park Place with Player 3, which would give both players dangerous monopolies. I cannot offer a better deal because I do not own Park Place.

I cannot stop Player 4 from trading Virginia and States to Player 3. I will focus on building houses quickly instead of trading. I am checking which unowned properties can be completed without buying from the bank first.

I am the only player with a completed monopoly right now. I must build houses before Player 4 and Player 3 finish their trades and monopolies. I will mortgage Indiana Avenue first for $110, then the utilities and Vermont, and finally build.

Player 4 is currently on Indiana Avenue, which I own. Mortgaging it now would not refund rent already paid this turn, but Player 4 just landed there and paid $18. The base rent is only $18, so losing that income is a small price to pay for raising cash.

I will mortgage Indiana Avenue first. I cannot mortgage any orange properties while they are still unimproved. Player 2 has cash and could buy Vermont to complete the light blue set, but Oriental is still in the bank so that trade is not viable.

I will not trade with Player 3 because they own railroads and could complete monopolies. I must build houses this turn to preserve my only monopoly window. Indiana Avenue is the highest-value mortgage first, raising cash to $272. That is still too little for three houses, so I will mortgage all four properties before building three.

Plan: mortgage Indiana $110, Electric $75, Water $75, Vermont $50 → $472; build 1 house each on St James/Tennessee/NY ($300) → $172. Thin vs $200 rails, but 3-house rents ($550/$600) are the win window; can sell a house if hit. Do not sell Vermont or Indiana. Do not mortgage orange."}
